document.title: Helios VEX - SIMATIC NET CP 1543-1 (CVE-2015-7547, source not collected)

publisher.name: Helios Industrial Security Lab
publisher.contact_details: Helios Industrial Security Lab, 42 Example Way, Springfield / vex@example.org

revision_history.summary: Source collection failed, so the status stays under_investigation; only a semantic estimate is offered.

full_product_name.name: GNU C Library 2.21 as a component of Siemens SIMATIC NET CP 1543-1 V2.1

notes.title: Vulnerability summary
notes.text: Multiple stack-based buffer overflows in the send_dg and send_vc functions of glibc allow remote code execution by way of a crafted DNS response.

notes.title: Basis for the VEX verdict
notes.text: The firmware image is vendor-signed and encrypted, extraction failed, and no public build recipe exists, so the source could not be collected (source_code_available=false). The code questions Q2-Q4 cannot be answered, so the official status of CSAFPID-0010 stays under_investigation. The semantic estimate and its evidence are recorded in analysis.semantic_estimation.

notes.title: Why the source could not be collected
notes.text: Firmware image encrypted (vendor-signed); no public build recipe; binary-only distribution.

semantic_estimation.rationale: The SBOM pins glibc 2.21, which sits inside the NVD affected range, and the module runs a DNS resolver on a routable interface, so the preconditions for the vulnerability are all met on paper. Nothing in the asset surface suggests the fix or a compensating control is present, so likely_affected dominates and the remaining hypotheses stay low rather than none.

evidence.value: DNS resolver reachable on the PROFINET/IT interface
no DNS pinning or egress filter in the asset record

hbom_evidence.relevance: Hosts the IP stack that goes through the DNS resolver, so the attack surface exists.
Manufactured before glibc 2.23 shipped, so a patched runtime is unlikely to be present.

threats.details: An attacker able to tamper with DNS responses on the path could achieve remote code execution on the communication module.
EPSS 0.89557 indicates very high exploitation likelihood, and several public exploits exist.

remediations.details: Pin the device to a trusted internal DNS resolver and block external DNS responses from reaching the control network at the perimeter.
With no source collected, impact is unconfirmed and no definitive fix instruction can be given until the vendor responds.
